updateCadence: Irregular, roughly monthly to bimonthly; latest stable release 153 (Sep 2026) while 154-156 issues are open
summary: A hardened Chromium fork carrying on Bromite with built-in content blocking, DoH and fingerprint-resistance patches. Runs on Android 8+, Windows and Linux; no extension support and no Play Store listing.
bestFor: Android users wanting built-in blocking without extensions
People who want a privacy-tuned Chromium engine

pros.title: Built-in blocking
pros.detail: Content filtering and DNS-over-HTTPS are included without extensions.

pros.title: Anti-fingerprinting patches
pros.detail: Carries Bromite-lineage fingerprinting and hardening patches (privacytools labels it Hardened).

pros.title: Open source
pros.detail: GPL-3.0 with patches public on GitHub.

pros.title: Modern Blink engine
pros.detail: Chromium 153 base gives Chrome-level site compatibility.

pros.title: Android, Windows and Linux
pros.detail: APKs for arm64, arm and x86_64, plus Windows zip and Linux tarball.

cons.title: No extensions
cons.detail: No extension ecosystem on Android; desktop extension handling not documented.

cons.title: Not on Google Play
cons.detail: Installed from GitHub releases, so updates are manual or via third-party repositories.

cons.title: Single maintainer
cons.detail: Privacytools notes keeping pace with Chromium security updates is a real burden.

cons.title: No sync
cons.detail: No account or sync mechanism and no DRM playback.

faq.a: No. Releases are distributed through GitHub (APK, Windows zip, Linux tarball).

faq.q: How is it related to Bromite?
faq.a: Cromite is a fork of Bromite created in 2023 after Bromite stopped being maintained in late 2022.
No extensions on Android. Desktop extension handling is not documented in sources reviewed.
